main_topics.reason: The user opened by asking why their A1C rose from 6.8 to 7.4 despite an unchanged routine.
The user described months of waking repeatedly, loud snoring, and feeling unrefreshed, then returned to sleep as a likely contributor.
The user asked whether age explained the increase and feared it meant diabetes was suddenly getting much worse.
The user asked what an individualized target means after their doctor had only said to stay under 7.
The user asked whether to get a meter and why morning and after-meal readings matter.
The user wanted a concrete plan for the next appointment rather than receiving the same vague response, and summarized questions to bring.
The user mentioned gaining a few pounds and asked whether it could affect blood sugar, but did not return to it.
The user said they had worried the result meant a sudden decline and later said they had expected things to be downhill because of age.

output.summary: The user asked why their A1C rose from 6.8 to 7.4 despite no reported routine changes and whether age was to blame; they also described broken sleep, loud snoring, and modest weight gain as possible contributors. The assistant discussed individualized targets and glucose monitoring and helped shape an appointment agenda, including a two-week food and sleep diary and questions about the snoring and a meter. The user said the conversation was more useful than expected, felt reassured, and restated the plan.
